questions.question: Which concept allows a class to acquire properties and methods of another class?
questions.explanation: Inheritance allows a child class to acquire properties and methods from a parent class.

questions.question: Which OOP concept hides internal implementation details?
questions.explanation: Abstraction hides unnecessary implementation details and exposes only essential features.

questions.question: Which concept means one interface can have multiple implementations?
questions.explanation: Polymorphism allows the same interface or method concept to behave differently in different situations.

questions.question: Which concept bundles data and methods together?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation combines data and related methods into a single unit, such as a class.

questions.question: What is an object in OOP?
questions.explanation: An object is an instance of a class containing its own state and behavior.
